claims.head: No wasted shots for the Canadiens
claims.call: The Canadiens’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Canadiens’ shots are some of the most dangerous in the league, and the Capitals are one of the worst at preventing dangerous ones. Look for plenty of good chances.

claims.head: Where the Canadiens have the edge: forecheck pressure
claims.body: The Canadiens are around the middle of the league for forecheck pressure, and the Capitals are near the bottom. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one.

notes.text: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Kirby Dach has taken his spot beside Alex Newhook and Juraj Slafkovský.
Mike Matheson is day to day (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson.
Oliver Kapanen is on injured reserve and has not played this season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 25% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 6% last season.
Pierre-Luc Dubois is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Dylan Strome has taken his spot beside Tom Wilson and Alex Tuch.

stakes: The Canadiens go in tied for fifth in the Atlantic with 7 points, the Capitals tied for fourth in the Metropolitan with 6 points.

WSH.head: The Capitals start a half-step behind
WSH.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Washington has home-ice advantage. The Capitals can tip it if they get good looks.

MTL.head: The Canadiens start a half-step ahead
MTL.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Washington has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Capitals can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Hutson against Hutson
